title: Hearing other big bands: Toshiko Akiyoshi - Lew Tabackin
summary: Herman criticises the Akiyoshi-Tabackin band's very long solos and sketchy writing.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: Big band discipline versus small-group freedom

blocks.x: Yeah. Do you feel that, say, the other existing contemporary big bands and generally speaking those that are not interested in exploring any new music, is that a enhancement or a detriment to what you're trying to do? Would more of them doing it be better?

I haven't really had enough time to try to analyze that aspect of it, because I go to hear whatever I can. Probably the most recent group I heard, well, this past year, six months ago, was the Toshiko Akiyoshi - Lew Tabackin band.
Yeah. And I was really quite shocked, only for one reason, because I kept reading these glowing reports about how beautiful the band is, and so on. And I

caught the band in Chicago and I -- I shouldn't be shocked, but I -- after reading some of these accolades, I'd like to know why her husband could allow such self-indulgent as 40-minute solos. I can't buy it, plus the fact the writing is all sketchy, it's written for the soloist after he's done, to give him a breath. That's the writing, to me.

I haven't yet found anything that's really structured. Like, if she has an Oriental piece, that they use some tape and then they go into something else and then -- and I will tell Mr. Pedder when I see him.
